pages.title: 01 // THE SCREEN-RECORDING TRAP
pages.content:
You want a 3D map video for your food vlog. So you open Google Maps. You screen-record your laptop screen. You manually drag the mouse. Your screen stutters.

Noticeable UI buttons clutter the frame. Your video looks amateur. Commercial maps are made for turn-by-turn driving. They are not built for 60FPS cinematic video production. VibePath replaces manual screen recording with automated 3D spatial flight.

pages.title: 02 // SOLVING THE 3-SECOND WEBGL CRASH
pages.content:
Why do WebGL canvas recorders fail after 3 seconds? Because browsers flush graphic buffers instantly to save GPU RAM. When camera flight moves faster than map tile downloads, you get black frames.

VibePath fixes this with two engineering laws:
1. Set preserveDrawingBuffer: true on the Mapbox instance.
2. Lock the flight into a Sequential 4-Stage Async Chain: Orbit (Zoom 1.8), Regional Descent (Zoom 9.5), District Scanner (Zoom 13.8), and Urban 3D Flyover (Zoom 17.8).

pages.title: 03 // 1-CLICK CINEMATIC VIDEO & ZERO FRAME DROPS
pages.content:
The browser links map.getCanvas().captureStream(60) directly to MediaRecorder. Recording triggers automatically at Stage 1 and stops 1.5s after Stage 4 locks target.

No screen recording tools required. No UI buttons in the final clip. Pure, unadulterated 60FPS 3D map cinema rendered straight from client GPU.
